clue.text: Had a get-together in spacecraft cut short

blocks.note: first meaning: joined up in orbit, as two spacecraft do
second meaning: trimmed, as a tail or wages are

explanation.surface: Astronauts held a meeting aboard their craft, but it was curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacecraft that link up in orbit are said to have docked, and a tail or pay that is reduced has also been docked.

clue.text: Money equally divided by six wanting to avoid conflict

indicators.note: a word split into two equal halves has room for something placed between them

blocks.note: dosh is British slang for money
Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Cash shared out evenly among six people who would rather not argue.
explanation.walkthrough: The four-letter slang word for money is cut exactly in half, two letters either side of the Roman six.
explanation.definitionFit: A dove is the emblem of peace, so a dovish politician favours negotiation over war.

clue.text: Study taken care of and maintained

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
looked after

explanation.surface: A study that has been well looked after and kept up.
explanation.walkthrough: Con for study is an old word, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert or argue it, which is what contended means.

clue.text: Property of landowners, say, in Mid-west

indicators.note: mid asks for only the central letters of the following word
one piece sits inside the other, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: the two middle letters of west
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A description of land owned by farmers in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-west reads as the US region, which has states; here it means only the middle of the word west.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large areas of land owned by one person or family, the holdings of the landed gentry.

clue.text: Number of staff available, holding captured enemy in half-hearted way

indicators.note: losing half of the heart means one of the two central doubled letters goes
holding means gripping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a manner is a way of doing something
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A tally of available staff, oddly bound up with prisoners of war and a feeble approach.
explanation.walkthrough: MANNER has NN at its heart; dropping one N is the half-hearted way, and the prisoner of war goes into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the workforce, the number of people available to do a job.

clue.text: Got arrested

blocks.note: first meaning: understood, as in 'I got it'
second meaning: taken into custody by police

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue sounds like a passive verb; split, both words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend is both to grasp an idea mentally and to seize a suspect, so the past tense fits each word.

clue.text: Nobility always poetically expressed in part of book

indicators.note: in places one piece within the letters of another

blocks.note: a page is one leaf of a book
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are forever described in verse somewhere within a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the titled aristocracy, so it is the nobility collectively.

clue.text: Turn with cry of excitement going over line

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece goes over, that is above, the other

blocks.note: an exclamation of delight
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone squeals with glee as they cross a line on their turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to swing round or pivot, as a line of soldiers does.

clue.text: Perhaps Odysseus conceals this ecstatic expression of feeling

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep something tucked away out of sight inside

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the Greek hero is hiding an outpouring of emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge; its last six letters join the first three of the hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is an effusive, enthusiastic outpouring, in speech or writing as in music.

clue.text: Excessive pride one's taken in any TV broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
taken in means admitted inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Television shows of any kind are full of conceited egotism.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity is an inflated opinion of oneself, pride carried too far.

clue.text: Things of passing interest in European article about odd MP here

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in an unusual order
about means surrounding, so the outer letters go round the rest

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
letters to be rearranged
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Short-lived trivia in a European newspaper piece about a strange politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are items meant to last only briefly, such as tickets and leaflets, now collected for passing interest.

clue.text: In some respect, a clever display

indicators.note: in some says the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Praise, in some ways, for a clever show.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a visually striking show or performance put on to impress onlookers.

clue.text: Stupidly put secret agent in most prominent position

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it badly and in disorder, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish spymaster placed an undercover operative in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: A spy in the spotlight is the joke; the two words supply exactly the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre stage is the middle of a theatre's stage, and so figuratively the place of greatest attention.

clue.text: Traveller's guide eventually abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text has been shortened, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: at last means eventually

explanation.surface: A travel guidebook that ended up being shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, which a traveller uses to find the way.

clue.text: Dig up seed scattered around end of plot that's detached

indicators.note: scattered things are spread about in no order, so the letters are rearranged
end of asks for the final letter of the following word
around means enclosing, so the rearranged letters go either side

blocks.note: to disinter is to exhume
letters to be rearranged
last letter of plot

explanation.surface: A gardener digs up seed spread around one end of an allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all gardening: plot, seed, digging. 'Detached' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterested means impartial, having no personal stake, which is being detached from the outcome.

clue.text: Blow absorbed by person with faith in analyst

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside another thing

blocks.note: a theist believes in God
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: A believer suffers a setback while having faith in a psychoanalyst.
explanation.definitionFit: Analyst is short for psychoanalyst, a kind of therapist who treats mental problems by talk.

clue.text: Period for Americans when this would be obvious advice to eater

definitions.text: when this would be obvious advice to eater

blocks.note: first meaning: the punctuation mark Americans call a period

blocks.clueFragment: when this would be obvious advice to eater
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: once you are sated, cease eating

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading: split into two words, the phrase tells a diner what to do when satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons call the dot ending a sentence a full stop, where Americans say period; the second half reads it as a diner's instruction.

clue.text: Student's strangely guarded nature

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an odd order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on a reserved young scholar's oddly cautious personality.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student who has not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: Elizabethan courtier who brought King Edward's predecessor

blocks.note: first meaning: a favourite at the court of Elizabeth I
second meaning, cryptic: King Edward is a potato variety, so its forerunner is the first potato brought to England

explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety, not a monarch; legend credits this explorer with introducing the potato to England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter, favourite of Elizabeth I, was a courtier, explorer and poet credited with bringing tobacco and potatoes home.

clue.text: Opposed to what, for the French, is old-fashioned

blocks.note: anti means against
que is French for what

explanation.surface: Someone against modern French ways calls them outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique describes something old, from an earlier era, and so out of date or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Authorised including Arthurian knight in dictionary

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
Sir Kay, King Arthur's foster brother, was a Knight of the Round Table

explanation.surface: A dictionary gives its approval to an entry about a Round Table knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve or sanction it, giving it permission.

clue.text: False statement about British pound giving offence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: an untruth
B is the abbreviation for British
L from libra, the symbol for the pound sterling

explanation.surface: An untrue claim about sterling causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False statement' looks like the definition, which it nearly is; here it is only the lie wrapped round British, with the pound sign added.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel, publishing a damaging falsehood about someone, is a legal wrong or offence.

clue.text: Flourish as learner in time of prosperity

indicators.note: in places one piece within the letters of another

blocks.note: an economic boom
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A trainee thrives during good economic times.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloom is to blossom, and figuratively to thrive or be at one's best.

clue.text: Turn aside, having frantically tried to break up fire

indicators.note: frantically suggests wild, disordered movement, so the letters are jumbled
something breaking up another splits it apart and sits in the gap

blocks.note: to sack is to fire from a job
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone desperately tried to stop a blaze and got diverted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames to be broken up; it means dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to divert from the main course, to steer someone off on a tangent.

clue.text: Like hot spots of current interest, containing resistance

indicators.note: to contain is to hold something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: topical matters are in the news now
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Trouble spots in the news, with an electrical circuit thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' and 'resistance' suggest electricity; hot spots are holiday places, not news flashpoints.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot holiday destinations near the equator are tropical, lying in the tropics.

clue.text: In East Germany, finally abandoned fairness

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word
in places one piece inside the letters around it

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
to quit is to leave or give up
last letter of Germany

explanation.surface: In the former East Germany, justice was at last given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Germany' reads as the old GDR, but the two words are used separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is fairness or even-handed justice, and also the legal system built on it.

clue.text: It's not bound to provide a little information

definitions.text: It's not bound to provide a little information

blocks.clueFragment: It's not bound to provide a little information
blocks.note: surface reading: someone under no obligation to tell you much
setter's reading: not bound like a book, a thin unbound booklet that carries brief information

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like obliged; it means stitched into hard covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small unbound booklet or leaflet giving brief information on one subject.

clue.text: First edition taken to cleaners

blocks.note: first place is the best
ED is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A first edition sent off to the dry cleaner's.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken to the cleaners is idiom for being thoroughly beaten, which is being bested.
